title: Freelance Facebook Ads Manager vs Agency: Cost Comparison
summary: Compare freelance Facebook ads managers with agencies on what each fee buys, how percentage fees scale with spend and what hidden costs to price before signing.
body_markdown:
## What does a freelancer cost beyond the fee?


Ask what shape the freelancer's quote takes. The table above shows the options: a flat plan, a flat retainer, or a percentage of spend with a floor. A freelancer can charge by the hour or by project as well, so ask for a monthly cap in writing.


Account changes cost learning time. Meta says an ad set stays in a[learning phase](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/112167992830700) until it can deliver stably, which it says usually happens after about 50 results in the week after the ad set's last significant edit. A manager who edits constantly, or who changes budgets every day, resets that process. Ask how changes will be batched.


Budget size also sets what the fee can buy. Meta's[minimum budget guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448) says that with a cost-per-result goal, your daily budget should be at least five times that goal. If your target cost per result is $40, that means a daily budget of at least $200 before the fee is added.


Creative is the line to price separately. A freelance buyer can run the account, but someone still has to supply a steady stream of new ads. Our guide to a[Facebook ads consultant versus a creative agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ads-consultant-vs-creative-agency) covers pairing the two, and the pricing of the creative line is the number to ask for.


## How do you compare a freelancer quote with an agency quote?


1. Put both quotes on the same scope: new ads each month, revisions, launches, tracking checks and reporting cadence.
2. Add the media budget and any percentage fee to the monthly total, and compare a three-month view, since setup fees fall in the first month.
3. Price the gaps: who makes creative, who covers absences and who repairs tracking.
4. Confirm ownership. The ad account, pixel and creative files should sit in your business portfolio, with the freelancer or agency given access.
5. Check the exit terms: notice period, any remaining fees and the handover of assets.


Then pick by what is missing. A freelancer is the better value when you already have a steady supply of finished ads and only need someone to run the account. An agency is worth the higher fee when nobody owns tracking, creative and reporting together.


## Where does Knowlify fit in a cost decision?


Knowlify prices done-for-you video ads and optional Meta campaign management by custom quote, with no public rate card. Its guarantee works like this: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund. The terms are on the[done-for-you page](https://knowlify.com/done-for-you) .


If your gap is finished video creative, Knowlify is our top pick. It can run the campaigns too, or supply creative only for a buyer you already employ, such as a freelancer. To compare a Knowlify quote with a freelancer,[book a scoping call](https://knowlify.com/book) with the same brief and budget you gave the freelancer. For the wider pricing model, read[Facebook Ad Agency Pricing: Fees and Budget](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ad-agency-pricing) .


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for finished video ads, priced by custom quote. Its guarantee is on the done-for-you page.
- Compare scope before price. A freelancer fee buys one person's time, while an agency fee may include backup, creative and reporting.
- Percentage fees with floors change with spend. In the published example above, WebFX's ongoing fee is lower below $23,333 of monthly spend and Adside AI's is lower above it.
- Media spend is separate from every management fee, so compare totals with media included.
- Price the gaps: creative, coverage, tracking repairs and the cost of frequent account changes.


## FAQ


### How much do freelance Facebook ads managers charge per month?


There is no standard published rate, and the figures on third-party pages conflict widely, so we do not quote one. Ask two or three freelancers to price the same scope, and ask each whether the quote is hourly, a flat monthly fee or a percentage of spend. Then compare the total, with creative and media included, against the agency formulas in the table above.


### Is a freelance Facebook ads manager cheaper than an agency?


It can be, but the comparison only holds when the scope matches. A freelancer quote that excludes creative, backup and reporting may need more budget from you. Compare the same monthly scope and the same media budget before deciding.


### Does the agency fee include my ad spend?


No. Media is billed separately: MetaAdsAgency says ad spend is paid directly to Meta, and LYFE Marketing recommends at least $500 a month in ad spend paid directly to Facebook. A management fee sits on top, and percentage fees are calculated on spend. Confirm in writing which charges the agency will bill and which go to Meta.


### How long should I commit to an agency?


Look for the shortest term that lets the agency complete a full test cycle. In the table above, Top Growth Marketing and Chamber Media are month-to-month, while LYFE Marketing starts with a 3-month contract. Balance the commitment against the switching cost, and make sure the ad account and creative files stay in your business portfolio either way.
